newsitem.title: INDIA: India says infiltration spurs Kashmir violence.
newsitem.headline: India says infiltration spurs Kashmir violence.

text.p: Indian army and police officials said on Monday that recent infiltration of militants from Pakistan has led to a fresh spurt of gun battles between separatists and security forces in troubled Kashmir.

"This is the season when militants infiltrate and there is more movement of the militants and the result is more encounters and more killings (of militants)," Brigadier General Ashok Kapoor of the Indian Army in Kashmir told Reuters.
Pakistan denies arming Kashmiri separatist guerrillas and says it provides only political and moral support to separatists.
Police said at least 36 separatist guerrillas and eight Indian security force personnel have been killed in gun battles in the last two days.
Indian soldiers on Sunday killed seven militants in a fierce gun battle near Gool in Udhampur.
"In an encounter with security forces at Gool, seven militants believed to be foreign mercenaries got killed," a police spokesman said.
Gool lies in the dense forests of Udhampur, 240 km (150 miles) north of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.

Three guerrillas and an Indian army officer were killed in a day-long gun battle in Srinagar on Sunday, a defence spokesman said. Three more militants were killed on Monday on the outskirts of Srinagar, he said.
Seven separatist guerrillas were killed in a shootout in south Kashmir by Indian security forces on Saturday.
"Over 65 militants were killed in the last 20 days and 121 militants were killed in the month of June," Kapoor said.
Militants on Saturday killed four Indian soldiers and wounded six others in a landmine explosion in the north Kashmir.
More than a dozen groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir, India's only Moslem-majority state.
Police and hospitals say over 20,000 people have been killed in seven years of separatist violence. Separatists and Farooq Abdullah, chief minister of the state put the toll near 50,000.
